evidence: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) with Bragg – Brentano geometry and Cu K a radiation was applied to study the phase composition of the films. The surface roughness was characterized using the atomic force microscopy (AFM) method. The concentrations of impurities were determined by the electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) method in the films grown on Si(111) substrates. The refractive index, thickness, and absorption coefficient values were calculated from the transmission spectra measured at room temperature in the spectral range of 190 – 850 nm for the films deposited on SiO 2 substrates. Room temperature and low temperature photoluminescence was investigated by using synchrotron radiation excitation at the SUPERLUMI station of HASYLAB at DESY. The absorption coefficient, a, of the films grown at 500 K, monotonically increased with the increase of photon energy, hm, from 5.7 to 6.4 eV (Fig. 3). The band-gap values of thin films have usually been estimated by extrapolating the linear parts of the ( ahm) 2 vs. hm [1,26 – 28] or (ahm) 1/2 vs. hm curves to a (hm)=0. The results of PL measurements, which will be presented later, indicate that the absorption maximum located at 5.9 eV may have excitonic origin.
